questions.question: What happens if a child class does not call super() in its constructor?
options: Compilation error if the parent has no no-arg constructor
explanations: Correct. Java inserts an implicit super() call, but if the parent has no parameterless constructor, it fails.
Java does it only if you do not write any super call, but it does not always work.
The parent is indeed initialized via the implicit super() call.

questions.question: In a hierarchy Person -> Doctor -> Surgeon, which constructor runs FIRST when creating a Surgeon?
explanations: It is not the first one.
Correct. The super() chain goes from the child up to the parent: Surgeon -> Doctor -> Person.

questions.question: Why is it recommended to use inheritance only for is-a relationships?
options: Because inheritance creates strong coupling and rigid hierarchies
explanations: Correct. Inheritance creates strong dependency. Composition is more flexible for has-a relationships.
Java does not require it, it is a design recommendation.
There are always alternatives such as composition and interfaces.
